historical_reviews.deepseek: Does not prove BRCM identity and omits the source-required target bus, speed and bandwidth evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires approved vendor/device identity, complete inventory plus target verbose output and secure read-only access.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A PCIe switch exposes an upstream port and multiple downstream bridges/functions; one generic bridge match cannot prove the switch instance or that every required port negotiates its assigned lane width. 'Bandwidth' must be normalized as link generation times lane count or defined throughput, not inferred from a product name.

original_test_intent: Verify the intended BRCM PCIe switch is present with the correct identity, topology and role-specific link speed/width or bandwidth against the platform SPEC.
original_method: Authenticate the exact SUT, resolve the approved BRCM vendor/device/subsystem identity and physical switch instance, collect complete domain-qualified inventory and topology plus verbose evidence for the upstream and required downstream ports, parse capability and negotiated link values, normalize the specified bandwidth metric, and compare without PCIe mutation.
manual_activity: A platform owner approves the exact BRCM switch instance, expected upstream/downstream topology and the meaning and limits of speed/bandwidth, then decides the verdict.
required_inputs: Physical switch instance and board mapping
Expected generation and lane width per port
safety_requirements: Collect complete unfiltered inventory/topology and target verbose context
Do not rescan, reset or reconfigure the switch or PCIe fabric
Preserve raw output and exit statuses
agent_execution_scope: Resolve the approved physical switch topology
Collect complete read-only inventory/tree and verbose port evidence
Parse IDs, BDFs, LnkCap and LnkSta
Compute only the owner-defined bandwidth metric
Compare each required port and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve switch instance and topology map
Approve ID, port, speed, width and bandwidth expectations
Disposition absent/extra ports and down-trained links

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A generic PLX/PEX/bridge grep may find unrelated bridges and proves neither the exact BRCM switch nor the source-required speed and bandwidth.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through verified-host SSH, capture complete domain-qualified lspci inventory/tree and verbose output for every approved switch port, then compare exact IDs and negotiated link values to the role-specific SPEC.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The BRCM switch PCIe identity/speed/bandwidth objective and 5-minute activity remain; complete instance and port evidence are added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Model the switch as one physical instance with an upstream port and an approved set of downstream roles, then compare exact IDs and link capability/negotiation per port.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces generic text filtering with exact numeric identity, topology correlation and an explicit bandwidth formula.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A single enumerated bridge can coexist with missing downstream ports or a down-trained upstream link; only the complete switch tree closes coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Theoretical link bandwidth derived from generation and width is not payload throughput. A traffic performance claim would require a separate workload and acceptance model.

project_override_considerations: Define the exact physical switch, all mandatory upstream/downstream ports, optional ports, accepted subsystem IDs, per-port generation/width and whether bandwidth means theoretical encoded link capacity or measured payload throughput.
expected_evidence: Verified target/host key and platform/firmware identity
Approved BRCM ID, instance and physical topology revision
Complete domain-qualified lspci inventory/tree and exit statuses
Verbose upstream/downstream port evidence with LnkCap/LnkSta
Per-port ID/speed/width and owner-defined bandwidth comparison

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target BRCM switch PCIe identity and link characteristics. DeepSeek's generic enumeration-only command is incomplete, not an authoritative conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The switch instance, topology and link SPEC are identifiable owner inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED only if exact physical mapping or the authoritative bandwidth definition cannot be obtained.

review_improvement: Expands presence-only grep into an exact physical switch and per-port topology/link contract.
independent_technical_reasoning: PCIe switches are fabrics, not single endpoints: the upstream bridge can enumerate correctly while a downstream port is absent or down-trained. Device/vendor identity must therefore be correlated to the whole approved switch tree, and any bandwidth number must state whether it is theoretical link capacity derived from generation/width or separately measured payload throughput.
